# FLUX.3-Action on Neuron

This plugin (`sglang_neuron`) runs Black Forest Labs' FLUX.3-Action DROID robot policy
(`black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-droid`) through SGLang Diffusion's own `Flux3ActionPipeline` on a trn2.48xlarge, with
BF16 weights, on torch-neuronx. From three camera frames, the robot state and a language instruction, the policy
denoises a chunk of future video latents together with a chunk of 32 actions, and returns the actions. SGLang's
[FLUX 3 Action cookbook page](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/cookbook/vla/FLUX/FLUX-3-Action.mdx)
describes the model, its request schema and its GPU deployment. This page covers what is particular to Neuron.

Three layouts are validated, each on 4 or 8 of the instance's 64 logical NeuronCores (LNC=2):

| `--model-variant` | Recipe | Layout | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sd` | step-distilled, 1 step | TP4 x CP2 | `--num-gpus 8 --tp-size 4 --ulysses-degree 2` |
| `sd` | step-distilled, 1 step | TP4 | `--num-gpus 4 --tp-size 4` |
| `gd` | guidance-distilled, 4 steps, no CFG | TP4 x CP2 | `--num-gpus 8 --tp-size 4 --ulysses-degree 2` |
| `gd` | guidance-distilled, 4 steps, no CFG | TP4 | `--num-gpus 4 --tp-size 4` |
| `base` | 4 steps, guidance 4.0 (video) and 1.0 (action) | TP4 x CFG2 | `--num-gpus 8 --tp-size 4 --enable-cfg-parallel` |

Other layouts, the FP8r packages and trn3 are not validated in this repository.

## The model

SGLang's preprocess, text-encoding, observation and denoising stages run as Neuron subclasses
(`NeuronFlux3ActionPipeline.create_pipeline_stages`), and SGLang's postprocess stage is used as it is. No tensor op
runs eagerly on the device. Each piece below is a compiled graph:

- **DiT:** SGLang's `Flux3Transformer` with a Neuron block on NKI kernels. SGLang loads and TP-shards the checkpoint on
  the host. Each stream's 5 mode blocks run as one compiled graph, and the 28 joint blocks as four compiled chains of 7.
  Each rank holds 1/tp of its sequence-parallel shard: the rows are all-gathered over TP before the projections and
  reduce-scattered after them. With CP, the video stream's attention
  uses the const-max ring kernel from `kernels/flux`. The output heads run inside the last joint graph.
- **Text encoder:** Qwen3-VL-4B's language model, one compiled graph per pad bucket of 80 tokens.
- **Video VAE:** SGLang's `Flux3VideoVAE` encoder with a tiled neighborhood attention in place of NATTEN, which has no
  Neuron build. Each Swin block is split over the TP group, which is one chip's four cores. At CP2, the first two
  stages' canvas rows are split over the CP pair with a window halo. The DROID canvas (the wrist view over the two
  halved exterior views) is built from the uint8 pixels in the same graph.
- **Sampler:** SGLang's Cosmos UniPC, with each step's CFG combine and update as one device graph. The coefficients
  come from the sigmas and config of SGLang's scheduler. At CFG2, each CFG rank runs its own branch and the step graph
  gathers both.

The models use SGLang's own TP, SP and CFG process groups, bound and checked by `runtime.initialize_model_groups` as
FLUX.1-dev's are. Each worker runs 4 torch threads.

The code is in `sglang_neuron/diffusion/flux3_action/` (the pipeline, DiT, VAE, sampler and text encoder), and the
block's kernels are in `sglang_neuron/diffusion/kernels/flux3.py`.

## Setup

The container and the SGLang checkout are the ones in the [setup guide](../getting-started/setup-guide.md). A container
must see the Neuron devices of the cores it serves on. Build the venv as for FLUX.1-dev. The script also installs
`websockets` and `msgpack`, which the OpenPI endpoint needs:

```bash
# from this repository's checkout under /work, as in the setup guide
NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES=0 scripts/setup_sglang_diffusion_env.sh /work/venv /work/sglang
source /work/venv/bin/activate
export PYTHONPATH=/work/sglang/python
export TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0
```

The commands below run in this venv: its `python` and `sglang` have the plugin, `websockets` and `msgpack`.

`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` is required for every launch, for the reason in the FLUX.1-dev recipe's
[runtime path](flux1-dev.md#the-runtime-path).

The policy package holds the `sd` and `gd` variants under `variants/` and the `base` policy at its root. The policy
config names its frozen components in `black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-base` at a pinned revision: the text encoder as
the `text_encoder` folder and the video VAE as `video_vae.safetensors`. SGLang downloads them when no component path
is given. To serve from local copies of that revision, pass them as components:

```bash
--component-paths.text_encoder /work/models/flux-3-action-base/text_encoder \
--component-paths.vae /work/models/flux-3-action-base/video_vae.safetensors
```

At the pinned revision, the `text_encoder` folder has the same 713 tensors and the same tokenizer and config files
(by SHA-256) as `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`. The accuracy results on this page served a local copy of
`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`.

Cores: worker `i` takes the `i`-th core of `NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, else of the launcher's `NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES`,
else core `i`. Each TP group is one chip's four cores when the list starts on a multiple of 4, as in every validated
run.

## Serving

```bash
sglang serve --model-path black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-droid --model-type diffusion --model-variant gd \
  --num-gpus 8 --tp-size 4 --ulysses-degree 2 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

Before the server reports ready, the pipeline runs one DROID request through its stages on every rank
(`NeuronFlux3ActionPipeline.warm_up`). The request has three black uint8 360x640 views, a zero state, and the package's
default steps and guidance. The first served request therefore compiles no graph. SGLang's default warmup builds no
request for an action policy, and `--warmup-mode request` warms only a one-step copy on a float canvas.

Clients use SGLang's OpenPI WebSocket, `/openpi/policy`, with msgpack numpy payloads: three uint8 360x640 views as
`observation.images.<camera>` (`wrist`, `left`, `right`, or the LeRobot names), the 8-dim state as
`observation.state`, and the instruction as `prompt`. The response carries the `[32, 8]` chunk as `actions`. The
cookbook page has the full schema.

SGLang's HTTP action API, `POST /v1/actions/generations` with `GET /v1/actions/metadata`, serves the same pipeline. On
`gd` TP4 x CP2, three uint8 views sent as base64 PNG returned the same actions as the WebSocket, with a longer round
trip. Pixel lists also returned the same actions, with a much longer round trip: the three views become a large JSON
body.

```python
import asyncio

import numpy as np
import websockets
from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.action.protocol import pack_msgpack, unpack_msgpack


async def main():
    observation = {f"observation.images.{name}": np.zeros((360, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
                   for name in ("wrist", "left", "right")}
    observation["observation.state"] = np.zeros(8, dtype=np.float32)
    observation["prompt"] = "put the marker in the cup"
    async with websockets.connect("ws://127.0.0.1:30000/openpi/policy", max_size=None) as ws:
        await ws.recv()
        await ws.send(pack_msgpack(observation))
        actions = np.asarray(unpack_msgpack(await ws.recv())["actions"])
        print(actions.shape)


asyncio.run(main())
```

SGLang's benchmark measures a running server:

```bash
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_flux3_action --url ws://127.0.0.1:30000 --warmup 10 --requests 100
```

### In the container image

The SGLang-Neuron container image ([docker/README.md](../../docker/README.md)) has SGLang, its diffusion packages
(`websockets` and `msgpack` included) and this plugin installed. Start it as
[docker/README.md](../../docker/README.md#run) says: the Neuron devices of the cores it serves on passed, the compile
caches mounted, and `-e TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` added. Inside it, the commands of [Serving](#serving) run with
these differences:

- No setup script, venv, SGLang checkout or `PYTHONPATH`: skip [Setup](#setup) except its component paragraph, and run
  `sglang` and `python3` from the image.
- The checkpoint: the examples assume the policy package `black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-droid` is in a host directory
  mounted as `/models/flux-3-action-droid` and the base components of [Setup](#setup)
  (`black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-base` at the revision the policy config names: its `text_encoder` folder and
  `video_vae.safetensors`) as `/models/flux-3-action-base`. Pass the package as `--model-path` and the components with
  `--component-paths.text_encoder` and `--component-paths.vae`.
- Give `sglang serve` `--host 0.0.0.0` in place of `--host 127.0.0.1` for clients outside the container
  ([docker/README.md](../../docker/README.md#run)).
- The Python client and the benchmark import SGLang: run them with the image's `python3`, for example with
  `docker exec <container> python3 <script>` and the script in a mounted directory.

The server, from the host:

```bash
docker run --rm --init --ipc=host --cap-add SYS_NICE \
    $(for d in /dev/neuron*; do printf -- '--device %s ' "$d"; done) \
    -v <models>:/models -v <cache dir>:/cache -p 127.0.0.1:30000:30000 \
    -e TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 \
    -e TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_DIR=/cache/neff -e TORCH_NEURONX_HLO_CACHE_DIR=/cache/hlo \
    -e NKI_COMPILE_CACHE_URL=/cache/nki \
    sglang-neuron:<tag> sglang serve --model-path /models/flux-3-action-droid \
      --component-paths.text_encoder /models/flux-3-action-base/text_encoder \
      --component-paths.vae /models/flux-3-action-base/video_vae.safetensors \
      --model-type diffusion --model-variant gd --num-gpus 8 --tp-size 4 --ulysses-degree 2 \
      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

## Compiled graphs

The first start of a layout compiles its graphs before the server reports ready. torch-neuronx caches the compiled
graphs under `TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_DIR` (default `/tmp/neff_cache`). Keep that directory across containers to skip
the compile. A worker refuses a cache that was built from other NKI kernel sources, as in the FLUX.1-dev recipe's
[Compiled shapes](flux1-dev.md#compiled-shapes).

## Accuracy

Measured on trn2.48xlarge with the validated container and the SGLang checkout of the setup guide, in one run: 16 DROID
observations against SGLang's own pipeline on the CPU in FP32 (the baseline) and BF16. A layout passes when the
Bhattacharyya coefficient (BC) of the error distributions is at least 0.99 or its RMS error is at most BF16's, with
every per-fixture L-inf ratio below 5 and L2 ratio below 3.

| Variant | Layout | BC | RMS ratio | worst L-inf / L2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sd` | TP4 x CP2 | 0.9944 | 1.109 | 1.86 / 1.55 |
| `sd` | TP4 | 0.9937 | 1.118 | 1.98 / 1.42 |
| `gd` | TP4 x CP2 | 0.9894 | 0.860 | 1.72 / 2.06 |
| `gd` | TP4 | 0.9845 | 0.816 | 1.80 / 2.11 |
| `base` | TP4 x CFG2 | 0.9899 | 0.821 | 2.56 / 2.08 |

All five layouts pass. `gd` TP4 passes on its RMS error, with a BC of 0.9845.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` | Required for a diffusion launch (Setup) |
| `NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES` | Core indices the workers take, in rank order. The first one set wins (Setup) |
| `NEURON_CC_FLAGS`, `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL` | Refused at launch when set. The DiT and the VAE pass their own compiler arguments |
| `TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_DIR` | torch-neuronx's compiled-graph cache (default `/tmp/neff_cache`) |

## What is refused

A launch that the pipeline does not serve fails before the server reports ready, and names the setting at fault:

- An FP8r package (`--model-variant fp8r`, `gd-fp8r`, `sd-fp8r`): `NotImplementedError`.
- A TP size that does not divide every VAE block's head count and MLP width, such as `--tp-size 3` or `8`:
  `ValueError`.
- An exported `NEURON_CC_FLAGS` or `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL`: `ValueError`. FLUX.3-Action has no compiler profile,
  so any value is refused.
- The platform's refusals for every diffusion launch: CPU or layerwise offload, SGLang's per-component placement, FSDP
  inference, torch.compile, the breakable CUDA graph, and a `--disagg-role` other than `monolithic` (see the FLUX.1-dev
  recipe's [What is refused](flux1-dev.md#what-is-refused)).

A request carries one observation and returns one action chunk. An `action_horizon` above the policy's 32 actions is
rejected.

# DeepSeek-V2 on Neuron

`DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite) runs on the [runtime](../design/runtime.md) on attention TP4, in bf16, as an
aggregated server or as a prefill and a decode server. The model is in `sglang_neuron/models/deepseek_v2/`.

## The model

The attention is multi-head latent attention, absorbed. A token's KV is cached as one compact row, its normalized KV
latent (512) followed by its rotated RoPE key (64), in SGLang's MLA pool on the NeuronCore
(`mem_cache/memory_pool.py`). The key side of the KV up-projection is folded into each query head, so the attention
scores the cached latents directly, and the value side turns each head's attended latent into its values
(`ops/attention/mla.py`). The prefill and the decode run the MLA kernels in `nki/`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  kv["KV down-projection, norm and RoPE key"] --> row["cached row: latent and RoPE key"]
  q["query, key up-projection folded in"] --> sc["scores against the cached latents"]
  row --> sc
  sc --> lat["attended latent per head"] --> val["value up-projection"] --> out["head values"]
```

RoPE uses YaRN frequencies, with the cos and sin scaled by YaRN's mscale over its `mscale_all_dim` mscale, and
DeepSeek's attention scale: `1/sqrt(q_head_dim)` times the square of the `mscale_all_dim` mscale, as DeepSeek's
modeling code computes it (transformers' version of the model leaves that factor out). The checkpoint rotates
interleaved channel pairs, so the loader reorders the RoPE rows of the query and of the KV down-projection into the
halves the graphs rotate.

The first layer (`first_k_dense_replace`, 1 for DeepSeek-V2-Lite) has a dense MLP. Each later layer sends each token
to its top six of 64 experts by softmax score (an exact reduction, not torch.topk on the device), next to two shared
experts. Each attention-TP rank holds a contiguous block of 16 routed experts and a TP shard of the shared experts, and
the two partials are all-reduced together. A decode runs the routed experts through nkilib's `moe_tkg`, selectively
for one or two rows and over every local expert above that. A prefill runs each local expert over the request's
tokens.

## Serving

The commands below run inside the container, with the checkpoints mounted at `/models`; the
[container guide](../guides/container.md) has the `docker run` for one node and for prefill/decode over two. The
[example](../../examples/deepseek_v2_lite/) has the prefill/decode layout and the aggregated server as scripts, and
[examples/README.md](../../examples/README.md#run-a-model) gives the order to run them.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-running-requests 64 \
  --max-total-tokens 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

`--host 0.0.0.0` listens inside the container; publish the port on the host's loopback only
(`-p 127.0.0.1:30000:30000`), as the [container guide](../guides/container.md#3-start-a-container) explains.

The MLA kernels and the runtime fix the layout:

- four query heads per rank: `--tp-size 4` for DeepSeek-V2-Lite's 16 heads;
- no DP attention (`--enable-dp-attention`), on any role;
- a decode context of whole 512-token tiles: `--context-length` a multiple of 512;
- a prefill window that fits in SBUF: `--context-length` at most 4096, the longest compiled on hardware;
- a prefill window that holds the whole request: `--chunked-prefill-size` equal to `--context-length`.

A prefill runs the smallest compiled window that holds the request, its cached prefix with its new tokens: one of 512,
1024, 2048 or 4096 tokens below `--chunked-prefill-size` (or the counts `--cuda-graph-bs-prefill` lists), or the chunk
itself. A decode step runs the graph of the smallest of a quarter, a
half and the whole context that holds its longest row; the decode kernel reads that context, rounded up to its
512-token supertiles.

Disaggregated, the prefill server and each decode server take the same model flags plus their role's:
`--disaggregation-mode prefill` or `--disaggregation-mode decode`, `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, and the
prefill's `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`.

```bash
# on the prefill node
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
  --host <prefill node> --port 30000
# on the decode node, one server per block of four NeuronCores (the next on 4-7 and port 30002)
NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES=0-3 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --stream-interval 4 \
  --host <decode node> --port 30001
```

Both use the image's NIXL, which carries the transfer's patches ([NIXL patches](../../patches/nixl/README.md)). A
balancer in front sends each request to the prefill server and to one decode server
(`sglang_neuron/disaggregation/balancer.py`, explained in the [disaggregated
tutorial](../tutorials/disaggregated-1p1d.md#2-put-the-balancer-in-front)), with one `--decode` per decode server:

```bash
python3 -m sglang_neuron.disaggregation.balancer --prefill http://<prefill node>:30000 \
  --decode http://<decode node>:30001 --decode http://<decode node>:30002
```

The tested layout is one prefill server on the prefill node in front of five decode servers side by side on the decode
node, each on its own four NeuronCores (`NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES`). `--stream-interval 4` streams each answer four
tokens at a time, so one benchmark client keeps up with every stream.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["client"] --> bal["balancer"]
  bal --> P["prefill server, TP4"]
  bal --> D["five decode servers, TP4 each"]
  P -->|"compact KV rows over NIXL"| D
```

The MLA pool's rows are the same on every attention-TP rank, so decode rank r takes prefill rank r's pages, moved as
whole pages of compact rows.

## What is refused

A launch the graphs can't serve fails at startup, naming the setting at fault:

- a launch off the layout above;
- an `--ep-size` other than 1: the routed experts split over the attention TP ranks, not over EP;
- a model dtype other than bfloat16 (`--dtype`, or the checkpoint's with `auto`);
- a `--max-running-requests` above 128, the most nkilib's `moe_tkg` takes in a step, or a launch without
  `--max-running-requests`, whose batch SGLang would size from the KV pool;
- a quantized checkpoint or a `--quantization`, or a checkpoint with a low-rank query (`q_lora_rank`), attention
  biases, routing other than greedy softmax top-k, renormalized top-k weights (`norm_topk_prob`), or a RoPE scaling
  other than YaRN;
- a KV cache dtype other than `auto`, `bf16` or `bfloat16`, a page size other than 128, and the features every model
  refuses ([What a launch refuses](../design/runtime.md#what-a-launch-refuses)).

# Qwen3 on Neuron

`Qwen3ForCausalLM` (Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-8B) runs on the [runtime](../design/runtime.md) in bf16, as an aggregated server
or as a prefill and a decode server. The host is `sglang_neuron/models/qwen3/sglang_model.py`; the graphs are the
shared dense transformer in `sglang_neuron/models/transformer/`.

## The model

Qwen3 is GQA attention with an RMSNorm on each query and key head (Qwen3's QK norm) before RoPE, which rotates the whole
head by plain frequencies, and a SwiGLU MLP whose gate and up projections load into one weight. Each phase runs its
attention in its own kernels:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Prefill
    pq["qkv_paged: QKV, QK norm, RoPE, K/V write"] --> pa["segmented attention over prefix and chunk, then out proj"]
  end
  subgraph Decode
    da["attention_block_tkg: QKV, QK norm, RoPE, attention over the row's pages, K/V write, output projection"]
  end
  pa --> ar["all-reduce over attention TP"]
  da --> ar
  ar --> mlp["MLP shard, then all-reduce"]
```

The attention heads, the MLP and the vocabulary split over the attention TP ranks. With fewer KV heads than ranks, each
KV head is replicated over an even group of ranks. The LM head stays sharded by vocabulary, and the device sampler reads
each rank's shard of the logits. A checkpoint that ties its LM head to the embedding (Qwen3-0.6B) loads one table for
both.

## Serving

The commands below run inside the container, with the checkpoints mounted at `/models`; the [container
guide](../guides/container.md) has the `docker run` for one node and for prefill/decode over two. The examples have the
prefill/decode layout and the aggregated server of each size as scripts ([Qwen3-8B](../../examples/qwen3_8b/),
[Qwen3-0.6B](../../examples/qwen3_0p6b/)), and [examples/README.md](../../examples/README.md#run-a-model) gives the
order to run them.

Aggregated, on four NeuronCores, with the validated flags for both sizes (Qwen3-0.6B takes
`--mem-fraction-static 0.4`):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /models/Qwen3-8B --tp-size 4 \
  --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 266240 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

`--host 0.0.0.0` listens inside the container; publish the port on the host's loopback only
(`-p 127.0.0.1:30000:30000`), as the [container guide](../guides/container.md#3-start-a-container) explains.

Qwen3-8B also serves at `--tp-size 8`, with the same flags otherwise.

Disaggregated, the prefill server and each decode server take the same model flags plus their role's:
`--disaggregation-mode prefill` or `--disaggregation-mode decode`, `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, and the
prefill's `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`.

```bash
# on the prefill node
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/Qwen3-8B --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 266240 --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
  --host <prefill node> --port 30000
# on the decode node, one server per block of four NeuronCores (the next on 4-7 and port 30002)
NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES=0-3 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/Qwen3-8B --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 266240 --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
  --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --stream-interval 4 \
  --host <decode node> --port 30001
```

Both use the image's NIXL, which carries the transfer's patches ([NIXL patches](../../patches/nixl/README.md)), and a
balancer in front sends each request to both (`sglang_neuron/disaggregation/balancer.py`, described in the
[disaggregated tutorial](../tutorials/disaggregated-1p1d.md#2-put-the-balancer-in-front)), here pointed at the decode
server's port 30001; give `--decode` once per decode server:

```bash
python3 -m sglang_neuron.disaggregation.balancer \
  --prefill http://<prefill node>:30000 --decode http://<decode node>:30001
```

The tested layouts put one prefill server on the prefill node in front of several decode servers side by side on the
decode node, each on its own four NeuronCores (`NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES`): five for Qwen3-0.6B, two for Qwen3-8B.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["client"] --> bal["balancer"]
  bal --> P["prefill server, TP4"]
  bal --> D["decode servers, TP4 each: five for 0.6B, two for 8B"]
  P -->|"KV over NIXL"| D
```

`--stream-interval 4` streams each answer four tokens at a time, so one benchmark client keeps up with every stream. The
[disaggregated tutorial](../tutorials/disaggregated-1p1d.md) walks through Qwen3-8B with one decode server.

DP attention on a decode server is served (`--enable-dp-attention --dp-size <replicas>`, with the DP identity's
conditions in [the serving policy](../design/runtime.md#the-serving-policy)).

## Compiled shapes

- **Prefill.** On an aggregated or prefill server (a disaggregated decode server compiles no prefill graph), a graph
  of the chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size`, one of the segmented kernel's KV segment tiles: 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 or
  8192) and one of each smaller token count `--cuda-graph-bs-prefill` lists (each also such a tile) or, without that
  flag, of each smaller tile that splits evenly over the attention TP ranks.
- **Decode.** A graph per batch size up to one scheduler's share of `--max-running-requests` (all of it without DP
  attention, split over the DP groups with it): the powers of two below the share and the share itself, unless
  `--cuda-graph-bs-decode` or the decode entry of `--cuda-graph-config` lists the sizes. Each compiles over the whole
  context and over a quarter and a half of it, and a step runs the smallest batch and context that hold it. A decode
  server with DP attention compiles the share alone, over the whole context only.
- `--max-total-tokens` sizes the KV pool, whose page count is a dimension of every graph; state it, so a relaunch finds
  its graphs in torch-neuronx's compile cache.

## What is refused

A launch the graphs can't serve fails at startup, naming the setting at fault:

- a model dtype other than bfloat16 (`--dtype`, or the checkpoint's with `auto`);
- a quantized checkpoint;
- sliding-window attention layers (`use_sliding_window`, or `sliding_attention` in `layer_types`);
- attention biases (`attention_bias`);
- a scaled RoPE (any `rope_type` but the default);
- attention heads that do not split over the attention TP ranks, KV heads that neither split over them nor replicate
  evenly across them, and an intermediate size that does not split over them;
- an `--ep-size` other than 1, since the dense graphs have no experts to split;
- a KV cache dtype other than `auto`, `bf16` or `bfloat16`, and a page size other than 128;
- the features every model refuses ([What a launch refuses](../design/runtime.md#what-a-launch-refuses)).

# Qwen3-MoE on Neuron

`Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` (Qwen3-30B-A3B) runs on the [runtime](../design/runtime.md) in bf16, as an aggregated server or
as a prefill and a decode server. The host is `sglang_neuron/models/qwen3_moe/sglang_model.py`: Qwen3's dense
transformer ([Qwen3](qwen3.md)) with a sparse MoE block in every layer (`sglang_neuron/models/qwen3_moe/moe.py`).

## The model

The attention is Qwen3's: GQA with the QK norm and plain RoPE, run by the QKV and segmented attention kernels in a
prefill and by one fused attention kernel per layer in a decode. Every layer's MLP is a sparse MoE block:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  h["normed hidden, every token"] --> r["router on every rank: softmax, top k, renormalized under norm_topk_prob"]
  r --> e["this rank's experts: moe_tkg in a decode, moe_cte in a prefill"]
  e --> ar["all-reduce over attention TP, the one that ends the layer"]
```

Every rank holds the whole router and routes every token, so no tokens move between ranks before the experts. Each
rank adds up its own experts' share of the routed output, and the layer's all-reduce sums the shares.

## Expert parallelism

`--ep-size` splits the experts into that many contiguous blocks, one per row of `tp-size / ep-size` consecutive ranks
of the attention TP group, and each expert's intermediate dimension splits over the ranks of its row. Without
`--ep-size`, every rank holds every expert and each expert's intermediate dimension splits over the whole attention TP.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph "--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2"
    a["ranks 0 and 1: first half of the experts, intermediate split in two"]
    b["ranks 2 and 3: second half, intermediate split in two"]
  end
  subgraph "--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4, the tested layout"
    c["each rank: a quarter of the experts, whole"]
  end
```

The expert mesh and its groups are in [Parallelism](../design/parallelism.md#qwen3-moes-experts).

## Compiled shapes

As Qwen3's: a prefill graph of the chunk and of each smaller KV segment tile that splits over the attention TP ranks,
and a decode graph per batch size up to `--max-running-requests` (the powers of two below it and the batch itself,
unless `--cuda-graph-bs-decode` lists the sizes), each over the whole context and over a quarter and a half of it. An
aggregated server compiles both families; a prefill server compiles only the prefill graphs, and a decode server only
the decode graphs.

## What is refused

A launch the graphs can't serve fails at startup, naming the setting at fault:

- Qwen3's refusals ([Qwen3](qwen3.md#what-is-refused)) except the dense intermediate size, since no layer is dense, and
  `--ep-size`, which splits its experts: a dtype other than bfloat16, a quantized checkpoint, sliding-window layers,
  attention biases, a scaled RoPE, attention heads that do not split over the attention TP ranks, and KV heads that
  neither split over them nor replicate evenly across them;
- dense MLP layers among the sparse ones (`decoder_sparse_step` other than 1, or `mlp_only_layers`);
- experts that do not split over the EP size, an EP size that does not divide the attention TP size, and an expert
  intermediate size that does not split over the ranks of its row;
- a prefill chunk the bf16 `moe_cte` kernel is not validated for, refused when the prefill graphs compile at warm-up.
  The limit depends on the expert intermediate shard (the expert intermediate size over the ranks of its row): a chunk
  of up to 8192 tokens with a shard of at most 768, up to 2048 with a shard of at most 1536, and none above that (more
  ranks per expert, a smaller `--ep-size` or a larger `--tp-size`, shrink the shard). Qwen3-30B-A3B's shard is 768 at
  `--ep-size 4`, so every chunk is served;
- DP attention (`--enable-dp-attention`), on any role;
- a KV cache dtype other than `auto`, `bf16` or `bfloat16`, a page size other than 128, and the features every model
  refuses ([What a launch refuses](../design/runtime.md#what-a-launch-refuses)).

```bash
  --max-running-requests 512 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 16 32 64 --max-total-tokens 65536 \
  --radix-cache-backend neuron-chunk --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mamba-track-interval 2048 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 2880 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-custom-all-reduce --trust-remote-code \
```

`--host 0.0.0.0` listens inside the container; publish the port on the host's loopback only
(`-p 127.0.0.1:30000:30000`), as the [container guide](../guides/container.md#3-start-a-container) explains.

- **Model path.** Use the text-only view of the checkpoint (`config.json` = the `text_config` as
  `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, every other file symlinked). The catalog does not serve the multimodal architecture.
- **Paging.** A launch is paged when `--context-length` exceeds `--page-size`. The catalog serves pages of 2048 (or
  256 / 512 / 1024) tokens at LNC 1. 2048 is the default: the KV page is then the tree's chunk, and with hardware-DGE
  page DMAs the paged decode attention costs what the slot pool's does, less than at 512 with spread queues (64 rows /
  16K). At 512, keep `QWEN35_ATTN_PAGE_Q=spread`: there hardware DGE and the compiler's queue are both slower. An
  aggregated DP-attention server is served because the megakernel plans each
  step for the whole DP cohort.
- **Chunk.** `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` is C = 2048 per replica (SGLang splits it over the 8 DP groups). It is the
  radix tree's page and the GDN checkpoint grid (`--mamba-track-interval 2048`). It must be whole KV pages and whole
  512-token blocks.
- **`--max-mamba-cache-size`** is the total over the DP replicas. SGLang reserves 5 state slots per running request
  with the extra buffer, so 2880 = 8 × (64 × 5 + 40 checkpoints). One slot is 12 MB per rank, so 360 slots per
  replica use 4.0 GiB. Raising it costs KV tokens (`--max-total-tokens`, per replica, 15 KiB/token/rank). A rank has
  about 10.6 GB after the weights. Each cached 2048-token chunk holds one checkpoint slot.
- **Decode batch.** `--cuda-graph-bs-decode 16 32 64` gives decode graphs of 16, 32 and 64 rows per replica (the
  kernel needs a multiple of 16), each at every context rung. The decode family compiles in nki's legacy mode
  (`runtime.DECODE_NKI_COMPILE_MODE`, NKI's instruction scheduling off), as the prefill family does. Under NKI's
  scheduling the 16-row graph exhausts the Pool engine's registers (NCC_IGCA094). The legacy mode costs the 32-row
  graph no step time (at 25 rows per replica).
- **Capacity at 2048-token pages.** With `--max-total-tokens 65536` per replica (32 pages), a request holds whole
  2048-token pages, so a replica runs at most 32 / ceil((prompt + output) / 2048) requests and the 64-row graph is not
  reached. For many short requests, use the high-concurrency recipe below.
- **Async.** The serving policy logs `async_execution: true`, with SGLang's overlap schedule.
- **Sampling.** Greedy only, no logprobs. Set `temperature: 0` (or `top_k: 1`) in each request. A request without a
  sampling field takes the checkpoint's `generation_config.json` values (temperature 0.6, top_k 20), and the server
  refuses it with HTTP 400. The chat template turns thinking on by default. For a chat eval, turn thinking off
  (`chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false}`), or give each answer 16K or more tokens and remove the stop
  strings that thinking text can contain (for example `Question:` and `Q:`).

## Launch for high-concurrency short prompts (pages of 512)

The same launch with `--page-size 512`, `QWEN35_ATTN_PAGE_Q=spread` (no `QWEN35_ATTN_SLOT_DGE`), and everything else
unchanged. A request then holds 512-token pages:

| Request (prompt + output) | Requests per replica, PG 2048 | Requests per replica, PG 512 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 512 + 512 | 32 | 64 (the 64-row graph) |
| 2048 + 512 | 16 | 25 |
| 8192 + 1024 | 6 | 7 |

The trade: at PG 512 the paged decode attention costs more per layer (at 64 rows / 16K), and at low concurrency TPOT
is higher (2k/512 and 8k/1k, both with the 32-row graph). At PG 2048, 2k/512 at c256 or c512 only queues.

## Routing (radix hits need replica affinity)

Each attention-DP replica keeps its own radix tree. A session's turns must reach the same replica to hit: use a
router with a cache-aware policy, or pin with `routed_dp_rank` in `/generate`. The in-server round-robin spreads a
session's turns over the replicas, so they never hit.

## Measured on one trn3 node

- **Numerics.**
  - GSM8K (250 questions, 5-shot, greedy, 64 in flight): 98.4% host-ids, 97.6% relay, 97.2% relay + direct submit.
  - Needles at about 12.8K tokens: 8/8 found, and each radix hit gives the same output.
- **Hit vs cold identity holds**, which is what caching needs. Radix check, 9.4K tokens: equal. AgentX session 0:
  6/6 turns equal.
- **Greedy outputs depend on what runs in the same step (a known property).**
  - The same server, one request at a time, twice: 40/40 identical.
  - One at a time vs 64 in flight: 23/40 identical.
  - A fresh server vs the previous one, both one request at a time: 26/40 identical.
  - Every step's MoE spans all 128 ranks, and the DP cohort's step mixes the replicas' rows (padding included), so
    the MXFP8 and accumulation order follow the step's composition, and which replica serves a request.
- **TPOT is device-bound** (8k/1k, 64-row decode over the full 16K span): it is the same at c1 and c8, the host
  trace puts nearly all of it in the decode program with the relay, and the host overhead with relay + direct submit
  is small. The decode attention over 16K pages is a large share of it, which the context ladder and the 32-row
  bucket target.
- **AgentX** (16 sessions × 6 turns, +512 per turn, c8, pinned): every later turn hits the whole 2048-token chunks of
  the previous turn. TTFT is lower hot than cold.
- **HiCache (L2 host) on the chunk-keyed tree.** Add `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2
  --hicache-write-policy write_through`. A HiCache page is the tree's 2048-token chunk, so the host KV pool holds each
  chunk's four 512-token device pages (1.90 GiB per rank); the GDN chunk-state checkpoints go to the state host pool.
  The prefill waits for the whole load (the KV and the state engines) before it reads the restored pages.
  Host memory: at `--hicache-ratio 2` with `--max-mamba-cache-size 2880`, each rank pins about 10 GiB (1.90 GiB of KV
  and 8.06 GiB of GDN state), about 1.3 TiB for the 128 ranks of a node. SGLang lets the host pools use all of the
  node's free memory but 10 GiB. On a trn3 node with 2 TB, this leaves about 145 GB free. Make sure that no other
  large host process runs on the node, or lower `--hicache-ratio` or `--max-mamba-cache-size`.
  Measured with sessions pinned to one replica (DP rank 2, 3 sessions of about 9.3K tokens, 9 fill prompts that evict them from
  HBM):

  | Path | Cached tokens | Greedy identical to cold |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Cold | 0 | — |
  | HBM hit | 8192 | 3/3 |
  | Host hit | 8192 | 3/3 |

  With `SGLANG_NEURON_HICACHE_VERIFY=1`, every load is checked against the device copy: 0 of 240 pages differ.

- **Decode context ladder and the 32-row bucket.** The cohort picks one context rung per step (4K / 8K / 16K pages,
  from the snapshot's longest decoding sequence). `--cuda-graph-bs-decode 32 64` adds a 32-row bucket. Measured at
  PG 512, before the 16-row graph (below), at 2k/512, 6k/1k and 8k/1k: TPOT is equal at c1 and c8, and at 8k/1k it is
  lower than with the 64-row decode over the full 16K span.

- **Replica position matters.** The same replica, one request at a time: 20/20 identical. Replica 0 vs replica 5:
  14/20. A request's replica changes its rows' place in the step, which explains the cross-server difference.

- **KV pages of 2048 tokens with hardware DGE** (the default above, in place of pages of 512 with spread queues). Same
  ladder, 32/64-row buckets, fresh compile: TPOT is lower than at PG 512 at 2k/512, 6k/1k and 8k/1k, at c1 and c8.

  - GSM8K n=250: 97.2%.
  - Determinism: the same replica 20/20, replica 0 vs replica 5 14/20 (as at 512).
  - The radix check passes.
  - HiCache: greedy output is identical on both hit paths (3/3), and
    `SGLANG_NEURON_HICACHE_VERIFY=1` finds 0 differing pages (a host load is now 4 pages of 2048 tokens).

- **The 16-row graph** (legacy nki compile mode, PG 2048, hardware DGE; one request per replica, c1 and c8 equal):
  TPOT is lower than with the 32-row graph at 2k/512, 6k/1k and 8k/1k, and at 512/512 at c64 / c128 (8 / 16 rows
  per replica). GSM8K n=250 98.0%.
  Determinism: the same replica 20/20, replica 0 vs replica 5 13/20. The radix check passes.
  The grid-edge probe passes: prompts one short of the grid decoding across it.

- **32K context** (`--context-length 65536 --max-total-tokens 69632`, same flags otherwise, HiCache on). The pool
  must hold the context plus two pages: the KV allocator keeps one page back, so with `--max-total-tokens 65536` a
  prompt near 64K tokens gets no tokens or is never scheduled, and the launch refuses that pool. The decode compiles 3 buckets × 3
  rungs (16K / 32K / 64K; the 32K and 64K rungs run single-pass split-K in the 60-layer decode). Prefill compiles
  3 prior tiers (0 / 16K / 64K).
  - Needles at about 27.3K tokens: 8/8 found, and every hit repeats the cold answer (26624 cached).
  - TPOT 32k/1k is equal at c1 and at c8.
  - AgentX: 16 sessions on 8 replicas, 7 turns, first prompt 8K, +4K per turn to about 33.5K. Later turns hit most
    of the reusable prefix, and their TTFT p50 is lower than a cold run's. Session 0 replayed cold matches its hit
    outputs on all 7 turns. 0 errors.
  - HiCache at about 31K prompts (2 sessions, then 2 fills that evict them from HBM but fit the 2× host pool):
    30720 tokens cached on both paths, greedy output identical 2/2.
    With 9 fills the host pool (133K tokens per replica) evicts them too, and the turn is cold.

- **Context past 64K** is not compiled. Contexts are powers of two, and 64K is the largest served and measured.
- **Prefill overlap.** A paged prefill forward runs its chunk as one micro-batch; the 1024-token overlap is a
  follow-up.

# GLM-4 on Neuron

`Glm4ForCausalLM` (GLM-4-9B-0414) runs on the [runtime](../design/runtime.md) in bf16, as an aggregated server or as a
prefill and a decode server. The host is `sglang_neuron/models/glm4/sglang_model.py`. The graphs are the shared dense
transformer in `sglang_neuron/models/transformer/`, the same one Qwen3 runs: [Qwen3](qwen3.md) describes its kernels
and its tensor parallelism.

## The model

GLM-4 is the dense transformer with four differences. Three are `TransformerConfig` settings that `glm4_config` reads
from the checkpoint's config; the fourth is the checkpoint layout `Glm4Graph` declares.

| Difference | What the graphs do |
| --- | --- |
| QKV biases (`attention_bias`, true when the config omits it) | the fused QKV projection carries the checkpoint's biases (`qkv_bias`) |
| Two more RMSNorms | one after the attention and one after the MLP, each before its residual add (`post_attention_norm`, `post_mlp_norm`) |
| Partial RoPE (`partial_rotary_factor`) | RoPE rotates the first `head_dim x partial_rotary_factor` channels of each query and key head (`rotary_dim`) and passes the rest through |
| Fused gate and up projection | the checkpoint stores one `gate_up_proj`, gate rows first (`fused_gate_up = True`); each rank reads its gate and up rows from the two halves |

Unlike Qwen3, GLM-4 has no RMSNorm on the query and key heads. One decoder layer:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  x["layer input"] --> n1["input_layernorm"] --> attn["attention: QKV with bias, partial RoPE"]
  attn --> n2["post_self_attn_layernorm"] --> add1(("+"))
  x --> add1
  add1 --> n3["post_attention_layernorm"] --> mlp["MLP: fused gate and up"]
  mlp --> n4["post_mlp_layernorm"] --> add2(("+"))
  add1 --> add2
  add2 --> y["layer output"]
```

The checkpoint rotates interleaved channel pairs (2j, 2j + 1), while the kernels rotate channel j with channel
j + head_dim / 2. The loaders permute the Q and K columns of the QKV weight and bias once, at load
(`sglang_neuron/models/glm4/rotary.py`), so the kernels run unchanged. q.k doesn't change when both sides get the same
permutation, and V is never rotated.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ckpt["checkpoint Q and K columns: interleaved pairs"] -->|"permuted at load"| cols["graph columns: contiguous halves"]
  cols --> kern["the dense kernels' RoPE, unchanged"]
```

(`-p 127.0.0.1:30000:30000`), as the [container guide](../guides/container.md#3-start-a-container) explains.

Disaggregated, the tested layout is one prefill server in front of two decode servers that sit side by side on the
decode node, each on its own four NeuronCores. A balancer sends every request to the prefill server and to one decode
server, and the KV moves between them over NIXL.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["client"] --> bal["balancer"]
  bal --> P["prefill server, TP4, port 30000"]
  bal --> D1["decode server, cores 0-3, port 30001"]
  bal --> D2["decode server, cores 4-7, port 30002"]
  P -->|"KV over NIXL"| D1
  P -->|"KV over NIXL"| D2
```

Each server takes the aggregated flags plus its role's: `--disaggregation-mode prefill` or `decode`,
`--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, and on the prefill the `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`. Both use the image's
NIXL, which carries the transfer's patches ([NIXL patches](../../patches/nixl/README.md)).

```bash
# on the prefill node
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/GLM-4-9B-0414 --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 266240 --mem-fraction-static 0.4 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
  --host <prefill node> --port 30000
# on the decode node, one server per block of four NeuronCores (the second on 4-7 and port 30002)
NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES=0-3 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/GLM-4-9B-0414 --tp-size 4 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 266240 --mem-fraction-static 0.4 \
  --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --stream-interval 4 \
  --host <decode node> --port 30001
# the balancer, with one --decode per decode server
python3 -m sglang_neuron.disaggregation.balancer \
  --prefill http://<prefill node>:30000 --decode http://<decode node>:30001 --decode http://<decode node>:30002
```

The [disaggregated tutorial](../tutorials/disaggregated-1p1d.md#2-put-the-balancer-in-front) explains the balancer.
`--stream-interval 4` streams each answer four tokens at a time, so one benchmark client keeps up with every stream.

A decode server also serves DP attention (`--enable-dp-attention --dp-size <replicas>`, under the conditions in
[the serving policy](../design/runtime.md#the-serving-policy)).

## Compiled shapes

The same as Qwen3's ([Compiled shapes](qwen3.md#compiled-shapes)). A prefill server compiles only the prefill graphs, a
decode server only the decode graphs, and an aggregated server both.

## What is refused

A launch the graphs can't serve fails at startup, naming the setting at fault:

- a model dtype other than bfloat16 (`--dtype`, or the checkpoint's own with `auto`);
- a quantized checkpoint;
- sliding-window layers (`use_sliding_window`, or `sliding_attention` in `layer_types`), which GLM-4 doesn't have;
- a scaled RoPE (any `rope_type` other than the default);
- attention heads, KV heads or an intermediate size that don't split over the attention TP ranks (KV heads may instead
  replicate evenly across them);
- an `--ep-size` other than 1, since GLM-4 has no experts to split;
- a KV cache dtype other than `auto`, `bf16` or `bfloat16`, a page size other than 128, and the features every model
  refuses ([What a launch refuses](../design/runtime.md#what-a-launch-refuses)).

# Wan2.2 A14B on Neuron

With this plugin, SGLang Diffusion runs Wan2.2 A14B text-to-video
(`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers`) and image-to-video (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers`) on a
trn2.48xlarge: BF16 weights, torch-neuronx, one 81-frame video per request at 480 x 832,
720 x 1280 or 1072 x 1920 (height x width), 40 steps. The model runs 4-way tensor parallel x
8-way context parallel x 2-way CFG parallel (TP4 x CP8 x CFG2) on the 64 logical NeuronCores
(LNC=2). Its defaults are those of the reference pipeline it is validated against.

## The model

- **DiT (both experts):** TP4 splits the 40 heads (10 per rank) and the FFN, and the residual
  stream is sequence-parallel over the TP group. CP8 splits the video tokens: 32,760 / 75,600 /
  168,840 at 480p / 720p / 1080p, or 4,095 / 9,450 / 21,105 per rank. Every rank keeps all 512
  text tokens for cross-attention.
- **CFG2:** the 64 ranks form two 32-rank replicas, each a full TP4 x CP8 DiT. One replica runs
  the positive prompt, the other the negative one. Each of the 32 CFG groups pairs a rank with its
  counterpart in the other replica, and one compiled graph per step gathers the two predictions
  over that pair and combines them.
- **UMT5 text encoder:** TP over all 64 ranks.
- **VAE:** ranks `0..size-1` for the patch-parallel degree `size`, in 32 x 32-latent tiles at
  stride 24.

The TP, CP and CFG groups are SGLang's own. On trn2.48xlarge they are placed on the 8 x 8 physical
mesh so that each group is a torus ring (`sglang_neuron/diffusion/distributed/parallel_state.py`).

## Setup

The container has Python 3.14, torch 2.14.0 and torch-neuronx 2.14.3, and must see all 16 Neuron
devices. Build the venv on SGLang `43881a7`, the commit in the
[setup guide](../getting-started/setup-guide.md); the plugin's SGLang patches refuse another:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang /work/sglang
git -C /work/sglang checkout 43881a7
# from this repository's checkout under /work, as in the setup guide
NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES=0 scripts/setup_sglang_diffusion_env.sh /work/venv /work/sglang
source /work/venv/bin/activate  # the venv's sglang and python
export PYTHONPATH=/work/sglang/python
export TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0
```

`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` is required for every launch. Without it, `import torch` in the
SGLang launcher autoloads torch-neuronx, which starts the Neuron runtime on every visible core and
leaves none for the 64 workers. The platform refuses to start when that has happened and names the
variable.

`--model-path` takes the Hub ID or a downloaded checkpoint directory, under any directory name.
Only Wan2.2 A14B checkpoints with BF16 weights run. The plugin refuses any other `WanPipeline` or
`WanImageToVideoPipeline` checkpoint (Wan2.1, Wan2.2 TI2V-5B, a quantized export) at model load.

## Serving

The layout is `--num-gpus 64 --tp-size 4 --cfg-parallel-size 2`. SGLang Diffusion sets its
sequence-parallel degree `sp_degree` to `num-gpus / (tp-size * cfg-parallel-size)` = 8, and the
pipeline uses SGLang's SP groups as its CP groups. CP attention is the plugin's own ring kernel over
each group; SGLang's Ulysses / ring split of `sp_degree` is unused. Leave `--sp-degree`,
`--ulysses-degree`, `--ring-degree` and `--dp-size` unset.

The VAE patch-parallel degree is fixed when the model loads. Set
`SGLANG_NEURON_WAN_VAE_PATCH_PARALLEL_SIZE` to the degree for the resolution you will serve:

| | 480p: `--height 480 --width 832` | 720p: `--height 720 --width 1280` | 1080p: `--height 1072 --width 1920` |
|---|---|---|---|
| T2V | 16 | 32 | 64 |
| I2V | 16 | 32 | 32 |

Unset, the degree comes from the first `--warmup-resolutions` entry, else 480p. A request at a size
whose degree differs still runs, with a WARNING.

For 1080p, request a height of 1072: I2V raises unless height and width are multiples of 16, and
T2V rounds them down. A request without a size gets 480 x 832.

## Compiled shapes

The first request at a new size compiles every graph. torch-neuronx caches the compiled graphs in
`TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_DIR` (default `/tmp/neff_cache`): use one persistent directory per
configuration, and give the first request a client timeout that covers the compile.

## Ring attention

At CP > 1 the DiT self-attention runs the const-max ring kernel
(`sglang_neuron/diffusion/kernels/wan/ring_attention_const_max_fwd.py`). Each rank keeps its own
K/V, and the kernel passes K/V around the CP group with `collective_permute`, overlapping the
exchange with the attention compute. The kernel has no online-max pass. It bounds each query row's
softmax maximum up front with a Cauchy–Schwarz bound, and because query rows do not rotate through
the ring, merging the ring steps is a plain sum.

No flag selects the attention path. Where the kernel cannot run (CPU tensors, fake-tensor tracing,
`SGLANG_NEURON_DISABLE_NKI_KERNELS=1`), the code all-gathers K/V and runs flash attention. Each
worker logs its choice once, at trace time:

```
WAN_RING_KERNEL=const_max ring_attention_const_max_fwd reason=eligible
WAN_RING_FALLBACK=allgather reason=...        (WARNING)
```

A run used the ring only if the workers logged the first line and never the second. With
`SGLANG_NEURON_REQUIRE_NKI_KERNELS=1` the fallback raises instead.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` | Required (Setup) |
| `SGLANG_NEURON_WAN_VAE_PATCH_PARALLEL_SIZE` | VAE patch-parallel degree (Serving) |
| `TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_DIR` | Compiled-graph cache (default `/tmp/neff_cache`) |
| `SGLANG_NEURON_WAN_SAVE_VIDEO_PT` | A `.pt` path. Rank 0 saves each request's decoded frames there as `[81, 3, H, W]` bf16 in [0, 1]. `{index}` in the path keeps one file per request |
| `SGLANG_NEURON_WAN_SAVE_VIDEO_PT_INDICES` | Comma list of 0-based request indices to save (unset: all). The save is synchronous, so keep it out of timed runs |
| `SGLANG_NEURON_VAE_MAX_DEVICE_GATHER_BYTES` | Size of one VAE output gather chunk (default 128 MiB). 512 MiB ran out of device memory at 1080p I2V |
| `SGLANG_NEURON_REQUIRE_NKI_KERNELS=1` | Raise when any NKI kernel, the ring kernel included, would fall back to torch |
| `SGLANG_NEURON_DISABLE_NKI_KERNELS=1` | Use the torch fallback of every NKI kernel |

Before the workers start, the platform applies `env_profiles.WAN22`
(`sglang_neuron/diffusion/env_profiles.py`). An exported value overrides any entry, with two
exceptions. The two CC DMA packet sizes are forced to 2048 with a WARNING. A launch that exports
`NEURON_CC_FLAGS` other than the profile's, or any `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL`, is refused:

```
TORCH_NEURONX_DISABLE_FALLBACK_EXECUTION=1
NEURON_RT_DBG_INTRA_RDH_CHANNEL_BUFFER_SIZE=167772160
NEURON_SCRATCHPAD_PAGE_SIZE=2048
NEURON_RT_DBG_CC_DMA_PACKET_SIZE=2048
NEURON_RT_DBG_CC_DMA_COPY_DMA_PRIO_PKT_SIZE=2048
NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2
NEURON_CC_FLAGS="-O1 --hbm-scratchpad-page-size=2048"
TORCH_NEURONX_PRESERVE_COMPILATION_ARTIFACTS=True
TORCH_NEURONX_DEBUG_DIR=./compile_dir
TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=3600
```

Both packet-size names are set on purpose, so NRT's start-up WARN on every worker,
`NEURON_RT_DBG_CC_DMA_COPY_DMA_PRIO_PKT_SIZE is specified, ignoring NEURON_RT_DBG_CC_DMA_PACKET_SIZE`,
is expected. The 3600 s lock timeout lets the other ranks wait while one rank compiles a NEFF.

## What is refused

- A launcher that has started the Neuron runtime: the platform refuses to start and names
  `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` (Setup).
- SGLang's CPU and layerwise offload, FSDP inference, `--enable-torch-compile`, the breakable CUDA
  graph, per-component placement (`--component-residency`, `--cpu-offload-components`,
  `--layerwise-offload-components`) and `--disagg-role` other than `monolithic`: the launcher
  refuses them at start, naming the flag.
- `NEURON_CC_FLAGS` other than the profile's, or any `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL`, in the launch
  environment.
- An I2V size whose height or width is not a multiple of 16 raises; T2V rounds it down (Serving).
- A `WanPipeline` or `WanImageToVideoPipeline` checkpoint other than Wan2.2 A14B with BF16 weights
  (Wan2.1, Wan2.2 TI2V-5B, a quantized export), at model load (Setup).
- Cache-DiT is not implemented.
- One prompt per request; several videos per prompt run one after another.

# MiniMax-H3 on Neuron

With this plugin, SGLang Diffusion serves `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` on a trn2.48xlarge, with BF16
weights, on torch-neuronx: one video with a stereo soundtrack per request, for two tasks:

- **t2va**: the prompt alone;
- **fl2va**: the prompt and a first keyframe, a last keyframe, or both.

The model runs 8-way tensor parallel (TP8) x 8-way context parallel (CP8) on the 64 logical
NeuronCores (LNC=2); its CP group is SGLang's sequence-parallel (SP) group. The pipeline is
`sglang_neuron/diffusion/minimax_h3_pipeline.py`; the model is in
`sglang_neuron/diffusion/models/minimax_h3/`.

## The model

One SGLang stage (`NeuronMiniMaxH3Stage`) runs the whole request on every rank in lockstep
(`NeuronMiniMaxH3Model.generate`):

- the Qwen3-VL conditioner, TP-sharded: its first 50 decoder blocks (the DiT reads the output of
  block 49) and, for each keyframe, its vision tower in FP32. Rank 0 loads the keyframes and
  broadcasts them to every rank;
- each keyframe's latent, encoded by the video VAE, tiled over the ranks;
- the denoise loop over one packed sequence of text, video and audio rows, video and audio on
  their own schedules. The checkpoint is guidance-distilled: each step is one DiT graph and one
  scheduler-update graph, and the latents stay on the device. The blocks' AdaLN projections
  depend on the timestep alone, so they are computed once per schedule and reused by the
  requests that share it;
- the video VAE decode, tiled over the ranks, and the audio VAE decode of the soundtrack, in
  FP32, in windows on ranks other than rank 0.

Context-parallel self-attention uses the NKI const-max ring kernel
(`ring_attention_const_max_fwd`). The blocks whose QK-norm gains exceed its bound on the softmax
maximum (45, 48 and 49) all-gather K/V instead.

The noise is drawn on the CPU from the request's seed, so it is the same on every host. Rank 0
records `TextEncodingStage`, `ImageVAEEncodingStage`, `DenoisingStage` (with per-step times),
`DecodingStage` and `AudioDecodingStage` in SGLang's request metrics.

## Serving

Launch with `--num-gpus 64 --tp-size 8`: `--num-gpus` is the number of workers, one logical
NeuronCore each. SGLang sets `--sp-degree` to `num-gpus / tp-size` = 8, and the model runs CP on
that SP group.

A request is SGLang's MiniMax-H3 request, offline and over `/v1/videos` alike:

- `task`: `t2va` or `fl2va`;
- `conditions`: empty for t2va; for fl2va one or two
  `{"type": "image", "uri": ..., "role": "keyframe", "frame_index": ...}`, `frame_index` 0 for
  the first frame and -1 for the last;
- `target`: `short_edge` (768), `aspect_ratio` (`auto` takes the first keyframe's) and
  `duration_seconds` (4 to 15; below 5, the shortest length the checkpoint was released for, logs
  a warning). 768, `16:9` and 5 s give 768 x 1344 and 124 frames.

Unset, `num_inference_steps` is 50 (at least 2). The output is 24 fps.

Python (`DiffGenerator`, run with `/work/venv/bin/python`):

```python
import numpy as np
from sglang.multimodal_gen import DiffGenerator


def main():
    generator = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained(
        model_path="/work/models/MiniMax-H3", num_gpus=64, tp_size=8
    )
    result = generator.generate(sampling_params_kwargs=dict(
        prompt="A golden retriever runs along a beach at sunset", seed=42, task="t2va", conditions=[],
        target={"short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0},
        save_output=True, output_path="out", return_file_paths_only=False,
    ))
    video = np.stack([np.asarray(frame) for frame in result.frames])  # T x H x W x 3, uint8
    audio = np.asarray(result.audio)  # 2 x samples, float32
    generator.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":  # SGLang starts the workers as subprocesses
    main()
```

```bash
/work/venv/bin/sglang serve --model-type diffusion --model-path /work/models/MiniMax-H3 \
  --num-gpus 64 --tp-size 8 --warmup-mode request --port 30000
```

## Compiled shapes

The DiT's packed sequence holds the text, keyframe, video and audio rows, so the first request at
a new canvas, frame count, set of keyframes or prompt length (in tokens) compiles its graphs.
torch-neuronx keeps the compiled graphs in `TORCH_NEURONX_NEFF_CACHE_DIR` (default
`/tmp/neff_cache`) and `TORCH_NEURONX_HLO_CACHE_DIR` (default `/tmp/hlo_cache`); keep both across
containers of the same image to skip the compile. Each cache records a digest of the NKI kernel
sources and the kernel library in its `KERNEL_SOURCES` file, and a worker refuses a cache with
another digest, or a filled cache without the file. To keep a cache that this checkout and image
filled before the file existed, record it with
`/work/venv/bin/python -m sglang_neuron.backend.compile_cache stamp <dir>`.

## What is refused

- At launch: CPU or layerwise offload, FSDP inference, torch.compile, the breakable CUDA graph and
  SGLang's per-component placement options; `--disagg-role` other than `monolithic`;
  `NEURON_CC_FLAGS` or `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL` exported with another value than the
  environment profile's.
- CFG parallel: the checkpoint is guidance-distilled.
- More than one prompt or output per request, fewer than 2 steps, the condition noise
  augmentation, Cache-DiT, Spectrum and rollout.

## Limitations

- The DiT graph is static in the prompt's token count: each new count compiles one more graph,
  and past Dynamo's recompile limit (8) a request at a new shape fails.

# Serving Qwen3.5-397B in P/D (1 prefill node + 1 decode node), radix cache on the paged pool

Status: **run on hardware**, 1P1D on two trn3 nodes, KV and GDN state over NIXL / EFA. Results
below.

- The aggregated server this builds on is in [Qwen3.5 radix](qwen35-radix.md).

## What each role runs

| Role | Graph families (`megakernel.ROLE_FAMILIES`) | Programs (`phase_programs`) |
|---|---|---|
| prefill | `prefill` | prefill, idle (an idle replica pads the cohort's prefill), no direct submit |
| decode | `decode` | decode, idle, direct submit |

What moves from prefill to decode over NIXL (SGLang's PD transfer, `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`):

- **KV:** the 15 full-attention layers' pages. `Qwen35SlotKVPool.get_contiguous_buf_infos` reports one entry per
  layer for K and one for V, and a page per item. K^T `[d, PG]` and V `[PG, d]` are each one contiguous 1 MiB page
  at PG 2048, so whole pages move by page id.
- **GDN state:** the request's recurrent and conv state of the 45 GDN layers, each slot whole through upstream's
  equal-TP path. Both nodes must run the same attention TP (16 per replica): the temporal state is stored in the
  kernels' `[k, h, v]` layout, which upstream cannot head-slice, so a pairing across attention TPs is refused at
  registration (`disaggregation/state_transfer.state_entries_problem`).

## Launch

Both nodes run the container image ([container guide](../guides/container.md): the node's network, the Neuron and EFA
devices, the checkpoint at `/models` and the weight pack mounted), with the same environment. In a development

`PYTHONPATH=<sglang-checkout>/python`, with the NIXL overlay `tools/build_nixl.sh` builds first (`NIXL_PLUGIN_DIR`

Prefill node:

```bash

```

Decode node:

```bash

  --max-running-requests 512 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 16 32 64
```

Front end, on the prefill node: the plugin's balancer, which the validation ran and the image includes (the
[example](../../examples/qwen35/) has it as `run_balancer.sh`):

```bash

  --decode http://<decode-ip>:30000
```

It listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and picks each request's prefill replica by load.

**Replica affinity needs another front end.** Both servers place a request on replica `bootstrap_room % dp`
(`follow_bootstrap_room`). The balancer picks the prefill replica by load, and SGLang's router (sglang_router 0.3.2,
not in the image) draws the room at random: it drops `routed_dp_rank`, rejects a client `bootstrap_room` (422), and
forwards `data_parallel_rank`, which the servers refuse as a room conflict; `--dp-aware` fails the same way
(502/503). Through either, a session's turns land on different replicas, so most of the reusable prefix is not
reused. A front end that pins a session to one replica on both servers (posting
each request to both with `bootstrap_room ≡ replica (mod 8)`) reuses most of it. This repository does not
ship that session-affinity proxy.

Launch notes:

- **Chunk.** The decode keys its radix tree on its own chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size` over its 8 DP groups), so
  both nodes take 16384, which is C = 2048 per replica. The decode's chunk must divide the prefill's
  (`sglang_patches.decode_radix_prefill_chunks`).
- **Radix on the decode** needs `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`. Without it, `--radix-cache-backend
  neuron-chunk` is refused on the decode.
- **Replica affinity.** Each attention-DP replica keeps its own tree on both nodes. A session's turns must reach
  the same replica on both nodes to hit, which the proxy provides.
- **Restart both servers together.** A stale NIXL peer breaks transfers.
- **Sampling.** Greedy only, no logprobs, as on the [aggregated server](qwen35-radix.md). Set `temperature: 0` (or
  `top_k: 1`) in each request: a request without a sampling field takes the checkpoint's temperature 0.6 and is
  refused.
- **Pool size.** Each role's `--max-total-tokens` must hold the context plus two pages (the KV allocator keeps one
  page back): 266240 on the prefill and 299008 on the decode at 262144. The launch refuses a smaller pool.
- **Compile.** Each role compiles only its family. Prefill: three prior tiers × the 2048 bucket (its warm-up reads
  the aggregated server's cache). Decode: 3 buckets × 3 context rungs (16K / 32K / 64K).

## 256K context: kv_cp=16 decode context parallelism

At 256K the decode's KV no longer fits one rank's whole pages (2 MB/page/layer × 15 attention layers × 128 pages
per request). The decode role then context-parallels the KV over the 16-rank replica: every rank holds both KV
heads of its 128-token block of each 2048-token page (1,920 B/token/rank), the PD transfer scatters each page's
block to the rank that attends over it (128 KB/page/layer per peer instead of 2 MB; 0.47 GB/request at 256K), and
the block tables, allocator and radix cache stay identical on every rank. The prefill is unchanged (kv_cp=1).

Decode node, as above plus:

```bash
SGLANG_NEURON_QWEN35_KV_CP=16 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  ... --context-length 262144 --max-total-tokens 299008 ...
```

Prefill node: no `SGLANG_NEURON_QWEN35_KV_CP` (the launch refuses it on the prefill and aggregated roles), and
`SGLANG_NEURON_QWEN35_KV_TM=1`, as in the validated pair above. The launch refuses `SGLANG_NEURON_QWEN35_KV_TM=1` on
any role but a kv_cp=1 PD prefill, and on a prefill without the paged pool (`--context-length` past `--page-size`).

- **Pool.** At 1,920 B/token/rank, 512K tokens would be ≈ 0.94 GiB/rank of KV (vs 15 GiB whole pages), next to
  weights+graphs 7.35 GB, GDN state 4.35 GB (TP16-sharded, unchanged) and 67 MB of RoPE tables. HBM is tight at
  that size; the validated launch sizes the pool at `--max-total-tokens 299008`, which still covers one 256K
  request (128 pages of 2048 = 262,144 tokens). The pool must also stay within the kernel's flat K/V write, or the
  launch refuses it: 15 attention layers x the pages of a layer (page 0 included) x 256 x the rank's block of a page
  must not pass 2^31 elements. A kv_cp=16 rank's block is 128 tokens. A kv_cp=1 pool of 2048-token pages, as on the
  prefill, holds at most 273 pages of a layer with page 0, 557,056 tokens.
- **Attention.** At kv_cp=16 a rank's share of 256K is 16K tokens, so the decode runs the unrolled attention path;
  the split-K block loop is the kv_cp=1 fallback and the >256K-per-rank case.
- **Transfer.** Each prefill rank sends only its KV head shard's block of each page to the two decode ranks that
  read it (sglang_patches/kv_cp_scatter); the equal-TP geometry (prefill attn TP = the decode CP group) is checked
  at peer registration ([the scatter](../design/context-parallelism.md#a-whole-page-prefill-into-a-cp-decode)).
- **State owner gate.** The GDN state is attention-TP sharded (kv_cp does not touch it), so a decode rank's state
  shard is on one prefill rank, its own in-replica index. The scatter gives every decode rank two KV sources
  ({e % 8, e % 8 + 8} at kv_cp=16), and only the source at the decode rank's own index sends the state; the other
  sends KV and aux only ([the state owner](../design/context-parallelism.md#a-whole-page-prefill-into-a-cp-decode)).
- **Prefill state pool.** In-flight 256K prompt KV is 3.84 GB/rank whole pages; `--max-mamba-cache-size 128` at
  dp8 bounds the mamba state pool accordingly.

# FLUX.1-dev on Neuron

`FluxPipeline` (`black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev`) runs text-to-image on SGLang Diffusion
(`sglang.multimodal_gen`), not on the plugin's LLM [runtime](../design/runtime.md), in bf16 on
torch-neuronx: 8-way tensor parallel (TP8) x 8-way context parallel (CP8) over the 64 logical
NeuronCores of a trn2.48xlarge (LNC=2, `NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2`: one logical core is two
physical cores). The pipeline is `sglang_neuron/diffusion/flux_pipeline.py`; the DiT (the FLUX
diffusion transformer) and the text encoders are in `sglang_neuron/diffusion/models/flux/`, the
VAE in `sglang_neuron/diffusion/distributed/autoencoders/` and the NKI kernels in
`sglang_neuron/diffusion/kernels/flux/`.

The tested launch is `--num-gpus 64 --tp-size 8` on a trn2.48xlarge. Other worker counts, other TP
sizes and trn3 are not tested.

## The model

One SGLang stage (`NeuronFluxStage`) runs the whole request on every rank in lockstep:

- text encoding: CLIP-L (on every rank) and T5-XXL (sharded over all 64 ranks);
- per-request DiT conditioning: the text tokens and every step's modulation rows (the per-step
  shift, scale and gate values of the DiT's AdaLN layers, computed from the timestep, the
  guidance scale and the pooled CLIP text embedding);
- the denoise loop; the Euler update is inside the DiT's last graph (at 4096 x 4096, where the
  DiT runs one graph per block, the Euler step is a graph of its own);
- the VAE decode, tiled over all 64 ranks; rank 0 then converts the image to SGLang's output
  format (float32 in [0, 1]) on one CPU thread.

Context-parallel attention is chosen by the joint token count: `(H/16) x (W/16)` image tokens,
for an image of `H` x `W` pixels, plus 512 text tokens. Up to 4,608 tokens (1024 x 1024), K/V
are all-gathered over the 8 CP ranks inside NKI kernels: `flux_gather_attention_fwd` in the 19
double-stream blocks; in the 38 single-stream blocks, `flux_gather_kv_fwd` then
`flux_gathered_kv_attention_fwd`, with the block's MLP running while the gather is in flight.
Above that (2048 x 2048 is 16,896 tokens), every block uses the ring kernel
(`flux_ring_attention_fwd`), which passes K/V from rank to rank.

## The runtime path

The SGLang launcher is the process you start (`sglang generate`, `sglang serve` or a
`DiffGenerator` script); it starts one worker process per NeuronCore.

1. **Activation.** SGLang selects the platform through the `sglang.multimodal_gen.platforms`
   entry point when torch-neuronx is installed (`sglang_neuron.diffusion:activate`). The
   `sglang.multimodal_gen.plugins` entry point then registers `NeuronFluxPipeline` for
   `FluxPipeline` checkpoints, replacing SGLang's own.
   The launcher holds no NeuronCore, and must not start the Neuron runtime:
   1. `import torch` loads torch-neuronx through its `torch.backends` autoload entry point
      (`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` turns that off);
   2. once torch-neuronx is loaded, the Neuron device is torch's accelerator, and SGLang
      Diffusion queries it at import, which starts the runtime on every visible core. The
      workers then cannot claim their cores.

   The platform fails at start, naming the variable, when the launcher has started the
   runtime.
2. **Launcher.** Before the workers start, the platform:
   - refuses the launches listed in [What is refused](#what-is-refused);
   - sets the model's environment profile (`env_profiles.FLUX1_DEV`: Neuron runtime collective
     settings, the HBM scratchpad page size, `NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2`, the compiler flags,
     `TORCH_NEURONX_DISABLE_FALLBACK_EXECUTION=1` (a graph that fails on the device raises
     instead of running on the CPU), the compile-artifact directory with its artifacts kept, and
     the compile-cache lock timeout) as defaults, which the workers inherit; an exported value
     wins, except for the compiler variables ([Environment variables](#environment-variables));
   - turns on Gloo lazy init (`TORCH_GLOO_LAZY_INIT=1`): each worker creates hundreds of
     process groups, and an eager full-mesh connect can fail intermittently;
   - caps the launcher's CPU thread pool at `cpus // tp-size`, where `cpus` is the number of
     CPUs the launcher may run on: an uncapped pool busy-waits on the CPUs the workers use.

   The platform reads `_class_name` in the checkpoint's `model_index.json` to pick the profile.
   Without the file (a local directory that has none, or the Hub unreachable with no cached
   copy; only the second logs a warning), it launches without the FLUX profile: none of the
   profile's defaults are set.
3. **Workers.** Each of the 64 workers claims one logical core, checks the compile caches (a
   cache built from other NKI kernel sources or another kernel library is refused; see
   [Compiled shapes](#compiled-shapes)) and only then imports torch-neuronx
   (`runtime.configure_worker`). SGLang then initializes `torch.distributed` with
   `cpu:gloo,neuron:neuron`: torch-neuronx's `neuron` process group sets up the device runtime,
   Gloo carries the CPU collectives. SGLang builds its own TP and sequence-parallel (SP) groups,
   TP8 x SP8, and the pipeline uses the SP groups as its CP groups. Before SGLang builds them,
   each worker renames SGLang's rank order onto the trn2 physical mesh (a hook,
   `sglang_neuron/sglang_patches/diffusion_mesh_rank_order.py`), so every TP and CP group is a
   ring on the chip torus (a trn2.48xlarge's 16 chips form a 4 x 4 torus; e.g. TP
   `[0,1,2,3,12,13,14,15]`). SGLang's scheduler on rank 0 hands each request to
   the other 63 workers.
4. **Metrics.** The stage records `TextEncodingStage`, `ConditioningStage`, `DenoisingStage`
   (with per-step times) and `DecodingStage` in SGLang's request metrics. torch-neuronx queues
   device work and returns, so rank 0 times the stages with device events
   (`torch.neuron.Event`), read after the image is copied to the CPU. They appear in
   `GenerationResult.metrics` and in SGLang's perf logs, and rank 0 logs one
   `[NeuronFlux] ... e2e_forward=...` line per request.

`--num-gpus` is the number of workers, one logical NeuronCore each. SGLang sets its SP degree to

```bash

  --num-gpus 64 --tp-size 8 \

  --output-path out --output-file-name fox.png
```

```python
        seed=42, save_output=False,
    ))

```

Server (OpenAI images API):

```bash

  --num-gpus 64 --tp-size 8 --warmup-mode request --port 30000
```

`--warmup-mode request` warms up with a 1-step copy of the first request, so the first request
compiles the 1-step graphs of that copy and then its own graphs
([Compiled shapes](#compiled-shapes)). A request (fields beyond the
OpenAI ones go at the top level):

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/generations -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
```

the CPU, so it is the same on every host.

SGLang turns each prompt of a list, and each output of a prompt (`n` in the images API,

after another.

matches the reference, but the image is near-uniform, so it is not useful for real images.

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|

| `NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES` | Core indices the workers take, in rank order; the first set wins ([Setup](#setup)) |

| `NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG` | The profile sets 2; the NKI kernels refuse another value |
| `NEURON_CC_FLAGS`, `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL` | Set by the plugin: the profile's flags for most graphs, the DiT's and the VAE's own for theirs. A launch that exports `NEURON_CC_FLAGS` other than the profile's `-O1 --hbm-scratchpad-page-size=2048`, or any `NEURON_COMPILER_OPT_LEVEL`, is refused |
